query: Loose Pages {A gust comes over the wall and takes a first-year's essay out of their hands, every page of it, and scatters it across the courtyard towards the fountain. They stand there holding the empty folder.|Wind, a folder, a first-year, and pages everywhere. The fountain looks hungry.|The pages are already in the air when you come through the arch. You know exactly where the fountain is.} Chase them down {You run them down one by one, off the flagstones, out of a hedge, one off a prefect's back. Every page, and only one of them damp.|You stamp on three, catch two and dive for the last at the fountain's rim. The first-year hugs the folder like a lost dog.|You read the wind and get to the fountain before the pages do, and catch them as they come.} {You get most of them. The last three go into the fountain, and you go in after the last one, and it's a long cold walk to the dormitory.|You trip on the fountain step and the pages sail on without you. The first-year helps you up, which isn't how it was meant to go.|The wind wins. You bring back half an essay and a leaf.} Lend them your own notes to start again {You sit with them on the cloister step while they work it up again from your notes. It comes out shorter and, honestly, better.|You lend them your notes and your afternoon. It takes all of it, and they tell their whole year you did.|You lend them your quill and your evening, and they hand it in on time.} Gather every page before it lands {Haste, and the courtyard slows around you. You pluck every page out of the air before the gust has finished, and hand back the folder neatly stacked.|You go round the courtyard like a whirl of wind yourself, and come back with the essay in order. The first-year counts the pages twice, then stares at you.|{spell_level(haste) >= 2: You catch the pages and the first-year's hat, which they hadn't noticed had gone.|You get every page but one, and that one you snatch off the fountain's surface, barely wet.}}
